title: 5 Best Durable Alternatives in 2026
summary: Durable alternatives compared on what's built in beyond the site and what each costs after year one: Wix, B12, Jimdo, GoDaddy Airo and Awesomic.
body_markdown:
Key takeaways:


- Wix and B12 are the only builders here whose own pages name all six extras we counted. Durable itself names five, Jimdo names five, and GoDaddy Airo names four.
- Jimdo puts bookings, payment links and a customer list on every plan, Free included, while Wix holds payments and bookings for Core at $29 a month billed yearly.
- Durable, Wix, GoDaddy Airo and Jimdo publish no plan renewal price, so ask every vendor, B12 included, for its renewal figure in writing.
- Awesomic brings AI agents and vetted experts into one app. Start with a prompt to build a website, app, campaign, deck or video, then switch models or bring in a vetted expert without losing the project context. AI-agent plans start at $19/month, and expert plans start at $1,799/month.[See current plans](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) .


If you're comparing Durable alternatives, you probably have a site already, so you're weighing what's bundled around it and what that costs after year one. All figures are US list prices, checked November 13, 2026, and some vendors localize prices by country.


Durable, now at durable.com after a move from durable.co, sells itself as an AI business builder: a site plus a CRM, bookings and AI agents, with paid plans from $22 a month billed yearly.


[Awesomic](https://www.awesomic.com/) leads the list because it's our product; it builds in none of the extras below, so read its cons before its pros. The other four are ranked by how many of six extras their own pages name (contacts or a CRM, bookings, payments or invoices, email marketing, an online store, and blog or SEO writing), with ties going to the cheaper plan that carries them.


## What changed at Durable in 2026


The biggest change is how Durable meters its AI. Launch used to list quotas such as 10 blog posts a month, and now each plan carries AI credits instead: 300 in total on Free "to try", 1,000 a month on Launch and 5,000 a month on Grow.


Prices moved as well. Launch costs $22 a month billed yearly, or $25 monthly, and Wayback Machine captures of the pricing page show Grow falling between June and July 2026 from $99 to $49, or $41 billed yearly.


Free got smaller. It now gives you a private preview rather than a public` .durable.site` address, so a business can't go live on it, and its CRM stops at 10 customers.


That leaves Launch as the real bundle: a custom domain, an unlimited CRM, unlimited bookings with calendar sync and paid bookings, and AI agents for blog posts, social posts, images, lead replies and Google review replies.


Invoicing is the odd one out. A March 17, 2026 launch post announced invoices with Stripe payment links, but today's pricing grid has no invoicing row. If you'd rather skip AI business builders and handle invoices in a separate tool, our[website builders roundup](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/website-builders) covers the wider field.


## Why owners look past Durable


Durable's own pages now name five of the six extras we count below, as many as Jimdo and more than GoDaddy Airo, so the reasons to leave come down to how far each piece goes, not what's missing.


The first limit is design and editing depth. Launch's card lists custom code, but the pricing FAQ says "we don't offer extensive options for HTML customization", so an AI-drafted site only bends so far, and in our view that's why sites in one trade can end up looking alike.


Selling is the second. Durable has added Sell, with a storefront, checkout and shipping, yet its pricing FAQ still says it's "not designed specifically to support e-commerce", and no plan on the pricing page names Sell.


The complaint predates Sell. In an r/website thread[weighing Durable against Weblium](https://www.reddit.com/r/website/comments/1rmuvu8/durable_weblium_other_options/) from March 2026, a poster who needed a buy button wrote that "Durable is good until it's not. It has a low limit ceiling", one Reddit user's anecdotal view.


Metering is the third: AI edits and AI posts now draw on one credit pool, so site changes eat into posts. A site needing custom logins or its own database may outgrow a site builder, though B12 and GoDaddy Airo list backends, and that's where the AI app builders in our[Emergent alternatives](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/emergent-alternatives) come in.


## The best Durable alternatives, compared


In the table below, the price is the lowest published plan, which isn't always the one carrying the extras in the last column.


Awesomic brings AI agents and vetted experts into one app. Start with a prompt to build a website, app, campaign, deck or video, then switch models or bring in a vetted expert without losing the project context. AI-agent plans start at $19/month, and expert plans start at $1,799/month.[See current plans](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) .


So read the last column next to Main limitation before you compare prices.


### 1. Awesomic


**Best for:** Owners outgrowing a lookalike site


**Overview:** Here's the gap first: Awesomic has no built-in CRM, invoicing or bookings, so we replace the site Durable made for you, not the back office around it.


You describe the business in a chat, and our agents build the site on the project's own cloud computer, then publish it to a live link in one click. Brand memory keeps your brand, files and decisions for every later job.


When looks decide whether a customer calls, a vetted designer on a separate All-in-One plan finishes the work. For that back office, you'll keep a Durable plan or move to other tools, and the agents connect to apps such as HubSpot, Shopify and Stripe.


We're backed by Y Combinator. Awesomic runs in a browser, with desktop apps for Linux, Windows (x64) and macOS (Apple Silicon), and on iOS and Android, where the iOS app lets you watch the agent work and preview the result.


**Key features:**


- A site live on the web with one click.
- 200+ templates as a starting point a designer can take further.
- 1,400+ app automations, plus MCP servers you plug in yourself.
- Projects you can share with a link.


**Pricing:** AI-agent plans start at $19/month, and expert plans start at $1,799/month.[See current plans](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) .


The fee is set in our Subscription Terms and covers every subscription, whether you joined from October 21, 2026 or earlier (earlier clients have paid it since November 1). Seats for teammates start at $19.99 each per month. The pricing page doesn't show either charge, so look at the checkout screen before you pay.


Experts are a separate purchase, and All-in-One, at $3,219 a month for design, copywriting, no-code development and quality checks, is the one for finishing a site. It includes its own Light subscription.


**Pros:** A designer can finish the site on an All-in-One plan, brand memory across jobs, browser, desktop and mobile apps


**Cons:** No built-in CRM, invoicing or bookings, no free plan or free trial, no refunds on agent plans, a floor far above Durable's $22 to $25 Launch plan once the Platform Fee is added, agent work spends a monthly AI budget, expert help costs extra


**How to start using it:**


1. Choose Light for the agents alone, or All-in-One if a designer should finish the site.
2. Read the checkout total before you pay.
3. Describe what you sell and who buys it.
4. Let the agents draft the site, then refine it.
5. Publish it to a live link.


**Why it's a good Durable alternative:** Agents and a designer can rebuild how the site looks instead of reshaping a template in Durable's editor.


**Final verdict:** Choose Awesomic when looking generic is costing you customers, and expect the All-in-One designer at $3,219 a month, not the agents alone, to make that difference. For a sole proprietor who mainly needs bookings and payments, Jimdo or Wix is the better pick for far less money.


To try it,[Get started](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) on Light, or on All-in-One for a designer from day one.


### 2. Wix


**Overview:** Wix ties B12 for the most ground here, and it wins the tie on price. Its own pages name every extra we counted: payments, pay links and invoices, scheduling, a store, a marketing suite with email campaigns, contacts and a blog.


The AI side is Harmony, Wix's builder with the Aria AI agent. The trade-off is lock-in, because a Wix support article says "you can't use another host".


Plan choice matters here. Light, the cheapest paid plan, has no payments line, so the plan that really compares with Durable's Launch is Core, which adds accepting payments, basic eCommerce and scheduling.


**Key features:**


- Store, payments and scheduling on one plan.
- Email campaigns and contacts in one marketing suite.
- Proposals with a signature step, which send an invoice once a client accepts.


**Pricing:** Free costs $0 with no card, and paid plans cost $17 for Light, $29 for Core, $39 for Business and $159 for Business Elite a month, under the note that "Displayed prices are for yearly subscriptions, paid in full at the time of purchase".


Wix says other subscription periods are available but shows no monthly-billed or renewal price. It offers a 14-day money-back guarantee and a free domain for the first year on your first purchase only.


**Pros:** All six extras named on its own pages, store and bookings on the same plan, a 14-day money-back guarantee


**Cons:** Payments and bookings start at Core's $29, only yearly prices shown, no outside hosting, no published renewal price


**What it does better than Durable:** Its store sits on a plan you can see. Core's basic eCommerce costs $29 a month billed yearly, while Durable's pricing page doesn't say which plan carries Sell.


**Final verdict:** Choose Wix if you want every extra in one place and are happy with the yearly prices it displays.


### 3. B12


**Overview:** B12 also names all six extras, but it splits them across two plans. Website covers the site, a custom domain free for the first year and B12 Commerce, which B12's docs describe as invoices and card payments in the US; its pricing grid ticks invoicing on every plan, though a help article files Commerce under Client Engagement. Website + Client Engagement adds a contact manager, client intake, email marketing, and contracts with eSignature.


That second plan suits service businesses that send proposals and contracts, a job Durable's pricing page doesn't touch. Bookings take some digging: B12's help center documents an Online Scheduling tool on Client Engagement plans, though the pricing page doesn't list it, and you can connect Calendly instead.


**Key features:**


- Contracts and eSignature beside invoicing on Client Engagement, so a quote turns into a signed, paid job in one tool.
- Client intake, a contact manager and scheduling on the same plan.
- An Expert Marketplace of designers and copywriters for pages the AI can't finish.


**Pricing:** Free costs $0 on a b12sites.com subdomain with 5 AI credits a day and no more than 30 in a month, and a limited-time offer lets new users try it for $1 for the first seven days. Website is $20 a month billed yearly, or $24 monthly, and Website + Client Engagement is $67 a month billed yearly, or $78 monthly.


**Pros:** Contracts and eSignature built in, invoicing on every plan per its pricing grid, designers and copywriters for hire


**Cons:** Contacts, email, scheduling and contracts need Client Engagement, done-for-you tiers carry a setup fee and can't downgrade, tiny free credits


**Why it's a good Durable alternative:** It covers the paperwork Durable doesn't, from intake to a signed contract.


**Final verdict:** Choose B12 if your sales run on proposals and contracts, and budget for Client Engagement at $67 a month billed yearly from day one.


### 4. Jimdo


**Overview:** Jimdo, from Jimdo GmbH in Hamburg, is the one builder here that puts most of its business extras on Free. Every plan gets payment links and an automatic customer list, and bookings are "free, with unlimited appointments", though events, buffers and reminders need a paid plan.


Its AI is metered differently, too. Companion AI gives you 50 messages a day with "No credits/tokens to buy", which is easier to plan around than a monthly credit pool, and sites are hosted in the EU.


Where Jimdo stops short is sending email. It collects newsletter sign-ups, and Companion AI can draft a campaign email, but there's no tool to send it. Companion AI also drafts blog posts and SEO text, though only Jimdo's blog stories say so. That makes five extras, level with Durable, at a lower entry price.


**Key features:**


- Unlimited appointments on every plan, so a salon or tutor pays nothing extra to take bookings.
- Payment links on Free, for getting paid without setting up a shop.
- A daily AI allowance with no credits to top up.


**Pricing:** Free costs $0 for 5 pages on a Jimdo subdomain, and Start, Grow, Complete and Unlimited cost $11, $17, $29 and $49.50 a month on a 12-month term paid upfront. Monthly terms cost more, with Start at $12, and Jimdo renews "at its regular price" without stating it; the free domain covers the first term only.


**Pros:** Bookings and payment links on Free, AI with nothing to buy, EU hosting


**Cons:** Free stops at 5 pages, support on Start replies within 2 business days, the shop needs Grow, Google Calendar sync is "coming soon"


**Why a sole proprietor might pick it:** It's the cheapest way here to take bookings and payments.


**Final verdict:** Pick Jimdo if you mostly book appointments and get paid for them, and you're happy to send email marketing from a separate tool.


### 5. GoDaddy Airo


**Overview:** GoDaddy Airo has the lowest paid price here, $9.99 a month billed annually on Starter. That covers Durable Launch's marketing side, with a free custom domain, marketing campaigns, social and blog posts, and getting paid by link or QR code, but not its CRM or bookings.


Professional is where it turns into a shop and an appointment book. It adds online payments and deposits, appointment bookings, a product catalog, sales tax, shipping and connectors including Mailchimp.


Airo's plan pages don't list a CRM, and its marketing campaigns build landing pages, blog posts and Facebook drafts rather than email sequences, which leaves it at four extras. Its AI runs on credits too, with 50 a month on Free for previews, and unused credits don't roll over.


**Key features:**


- Code download as a zip, per a GoDaddy help article.
- Online payments, deposits and a product catalog on Professional.
- Sales tax and shipping settings.


**Pricing:** Free is $0, and Starter, Professional and Ultimate cost $9.99, $24.99 and $99.99 a month billed annually, with monthly billing also offered. GoDaddy's "renews at current prices" note covers the free domain, and it publishes no plan renewal price.


**Pros:** The lowest paid price here, code you can download, bookings and a catalog on one plan


**Cons:** No published renewal price, Starter has one site and no bookings, no CRM listed, "Remove Airo branding" is still "coming soon"


**Where it pulls ahead of Wix:** Your site's code comes out as a zip, so leaving later doesn't mean starting again from a blank page.


**Final verdict:** Pick GoDaddy Airo for a cheap year of marketing and payments, and ask what it renews at before you commit to a second.


## What's built in beyond the site


The NFIB, the small-business trade association, found in its 2025[Small Business and Technology](https://www.nfib.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/2025-NFIB-Technology-Survey.pdf) survey that "Overall, 82% of small businesses have their own website", and that of those, "about a fifth (19%) accept payments through their website, while 81% do not."


So most small businesses with a site don't take payments on it, and a bundle's payments line is worth less than it looks unless you sell online. The table shows what each vendor's own pages name, with the starting plan where given.


Extra Durable Wix B12 Jimdo GoDaddy Airo Awesomic


Contacts or CRM Launch; Free capped at 10 Contacts Client Engagement Every plan Not listed Not built in; connects to HubSpot


Bookings Sync and paid bookings on Launch Core Client Engagement, per help center Every plan Professional Not built in


Payments or invoices Paid bookings; invoices per launch post Core for payments Commerce on Website Payment links, every plan Pay links on Starter Not built in; connects to Stripe


Email marketing Not listed Email campaigns Client Engagement No sending tool Not listed Not built in; expert plans


Online store Durable Sell; plan not stated Core Commerce on Website Grow Catalog on Professional Not built in; connects to Shopify


Blog or SEO writing Blog agent on Launch Blog Named Companion AI drafts posts Blog posts on Starter Not built in; expert plans


Extras named 5 6 6 5 4 0 built in


Wix and B12 are the only columns naming all six, though B12's scheduling lives in its help center, and Jimdo is the only one whose pages clearly put both bookings and payments on a free plan.


If none of these rows matters because the business runs on referrals, the design-led builders in our[Framer alternatives roundup](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/framer-alternatives) are a better place to start.


## What each costs in year one and after


Sticker prices don't compare. Wix and Jimdo list prices for a year paid upfront, though both sell other terms. Airo, Durable and B12 bill monthly or yearly, and Awesomic bills monthly. This table is our arithmetic at list price for the cheapest paid plan carrying payments and bookings, or the nearest match.


Builder Plan Billing Year one at list price After year one


Durable Launch $22/month yearly, or $25 monthly $264 yearly, or $300 monthly No renewal price published


Wix Core Yearly, paid upfront $348 No renewal price shown


B12 Website + Client Engagement $67/month yearly, or $78 monthly $804 yearly, or $936 monthly Free domain ends; ask for renewal terms


Jimdo Start 12-month term, paid upfront $132 "At its regular price", not stated


GoDaddy Airo Professional Billed annually $299.88 No plan renewal price published


Awesomic Light + Platform Fee, one person Monthly $2,628, our math No price change announced


Jimdo's Start is the cheapest first year at $132, and Durable is second at $264 billed yearly. Durable's October 20, 2026 Terms call fees "non-cancelable and non-refundable" unless your account says otherwise, yet its upgrade screen shows a 30-day guarantee. B12 is the priciest of the four alternative builders because its scheduling, contacts and email sit on Client Engagement. Awesomic's $2,628 is higher still, mostly the Platform Fee, before any seat, CRM or booking tool.


Credits are the cost the table can't show. In an r/webdesign thread about[credit-metered AI builders](https://www.reddit.com/r/webdesign/comments/1tjar1p/ai_website_builders_are_great_until_you_need_to/) , the poster, who built on Hostinger Horizons and names Durable among others, wrote that "Every small edit eats credits" and "The build phase is cheap but the grow phase is where they get you", an anecdotal Reddit take. If 10Web, another AI builder, is on your shortlist, ask how it charges for edits, and our[10Web alternatives](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/10web-alternatives) roundup covers its rivals.


## Taking your domain, content and customers with you


Leaving Durable takes longer than joining it, mostly because of the domain. Its pricing FAQ says moving a domain out "takes a couple of weeks" and "has a minimum subscription time", so start about a month before renewal and work in this order:


1. Ask Durable to transfer your domain while your plan is active, and confirm when the minimum term ends.
2. Get your customer list out of the CRM before you downgrade, because Free caps it at 10 customers.
3. Copy every page's text, your images and your blog posts into a folder you control.
4. List your booking services, durations and prices, then rebuild them on the new tool.
5. Re-create any payment links, and tell repeat customers which link to use.
6. Test the new site on its temporary address, then point the domain once the transfer lands.


Step 4 is where plans bite. Bookings need Wix Core or Airo's Professional, B12's scheduling sits on Client Engagement, Jimdo's Google Calendar sync is still "coming soon", and Awesomic has no booking tool, so bookings move to a separate app. To rebuild by hand with full design control, our[Webflow alternatives roundup](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/webflow-alternatives) compares the visual builders made for that.


## How to choose by business type


Start with the job that eats your week. If you book appointments, as a salon, tutor or trades business does, Jimdo gives you bookings and payment links on every plan and a shop from Grow at $17, while Wix Core puts a store, payments and bookings on one $29 plan.


If you sell products, Wix Core, B12's Website plan, Jimdo Grow and GoDaddy Airo's Professional all carry a store, and Airo's page also names sales tax and shipping. If you send proposals, B12 bundles contracts and eSignature with invoicing, and Wix has Proposals with a signature step. If marketing is the whole job, Airo's Starter covers campaigns, posts and pay-by-link for $9.99 a month billed annually.


Looks are the last case. In Information Processing & Management,[Robins and Holmes (2008)](https://www.makinggood.ac.nz/media/1276/robinsholmes_2008_aestheticsandcredibilityinwebdesign.pdf) had 20 subjects make 840 credibility judgments on pages with identical content, shown one at a time, and "the content with a higher aesthetic treatment was judged as having higher credibility", with each judgment taking about 3.4 seconds on average.


So a plainer-looking site starts behind on trust whatever it says, as our piece on[templates versus custom design](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/website-templates-vs-custom-design) explains, and that's the case where we fit.


## Picking your Durable replacement this week


Pick the one extra you'd miss most, find its row in the built-in table, then check the cost table for the plan that carries it and shortlist the two cheapest. Build the same three pages on each, using Wix's or Jimdo's Free plan or B12's limited-time $1 first week, and compare what each charges at checkout before you commit to a year.


Keep Durable running until the domain transfer lands and your bookings work on the new site. If design is why you're leaving, our[Durable comparison](https://www.awesomic.com/alternatives/durable-alternative) sets Awesomic and Durable side by side.


## FAQ


### Is Durable free to use?


Durable's Free plan costs $0 but no longer publishes a public site. You get a private preview and 300 AI credits in total, so going live on your own domain means paying for Launch, which costs $25 monthly or $22 a month billed yearly.


### Does Durable include invoicing?


Durable announced invoices with Stripe payment links in a March 17, 2026 launch post, but the current pricing grid has no invoicing row, so ask which plan includes it. Among the alternatives to Durable, B12 Commerce handles invoices and card payments, listed on its Website card at $20 a month billed yearly (its help center files them under Client Engagement), and Wix's pages also name invoices, though not which plan carries them.


### Which Durable alternative is best for an online store?


Wix, from Core at $29 a month billed yearly, adds basic eCommerce beside payments and scheduling. Jimdo's shop starts at Grow for $17 a month on a 12-month term, B12 lists commerce from its Website plan, and GoDaddy Airo's Professional adds a product catalog with sales tax and shipping.


### Can I keep my domain if I leave Durable?


Yes, though Durable's FAQ warns that a transfer out takes about two weeks and carries a minimum subscription time. Start well before renewal, and ask Durable about refunds, because its Terms make fees non-refundable unless your account says otherwise.


### Which alternatives to Durable cost least after the first year?


Nobody can say for certain, since none of Durable, Wix, GoDaddy Airo or Jimdo prints a plan renewal price. For year one at list price, Jimdo's Start at $132 for a 12-month term is the cheapest paid plan with bookings and payment links. Get renewal terms from each vendor in writing, B12's too.
